servers.description: List of IMAP servers to connect to. Each server defines credentials and connection details.

name.description: Identifier for this server (used in rules and account definitions). Must be a valid Lua identifier.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the IMAP server.

port.description: IMAP port number (typically 143 for non-SSL, 993 for SSL).

ssl.description: Enable SSL/TLS encryption for the connection.

password.description: Password for IMAP authentication. Use secure storage (e.g., keyring) in production.

auth_type.description: Authentication mechanism (e.g., 'PLAIN', 'LOGIN', 'CRAM-MD5'). If omitted, defaults to server-supported.

logfile.description: Path to the log file for IMAPFilter. Supports tilde (~) expansion for home directory.

timeout.description: Connection and command timeout in seconds.

poll.description: Poll interval in seconds when running in daemon mode.

subscribe.description: Automatically subscribe to newly created mailboxes.

create_folders.description: Automatically create mailboxes that do not exist (required only for some servers).

accounts.description: List of accounts with their filtering rules. Each account references one server name and defines rules to apply to messages.

server_name.description: Name of the server (as defined in `servers`) to apply these rules against.

rules.description: List of filtering rules to apply for this account.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the rule does.

condition.description: Lua expression returning boolean. Uses IMAPFilter's pattern-matching functions (e.g., `is_from`, `is_subject`, `is_header`, etc.).

move_to.description: Mailbox name to move matching messages to (must exist on the server).

mark_seen.description: If true, mark matching messages as seen.

forward_to.description: List of email addresses to forward matching messages to.

copy_to.description: Mailbox name to copy matching messages to (instead of moving).

set_flags.description: List of IMAP flags to set on matching messages (e.g., 'Seen', 'Flagged', 'Answered').
